source_title: Paul Anthony Kelly Had 1 Hour to Learn Tango with Jessica Lange for ‘American Horror Story’ - People.com
source_excerpt:
The actor tells PEOPLE that neither he nor Lange knew how to tango before filming their scene together, leading to plenty of laughs and missteps on set
Paul Anthony Kelly tells PEOPLE he and Jessica Lange had about one hour to learn the tango before filming their American Horror Story scene
Kelly, who plays the Devil opposite Lange’s Constance Langdon, admits he had no prior dance experience
The actor recalls laughing through their missteps and calls working alongside the actress a “great gift”
Paul Anthony Kelly had to think fast on his feet while filming American Horror Story alongside Jessica Lange .
The actor, who plays the Devil in the show’s 13th season, tells PEOPLE that he and Lange had very little time to master the choreography before filming their scene together.
“The tango-dancing, I think, was probably the most challenging, ’cause neither of us knew how to tango yet,” Kelly tells PEOPLE ahead of the season 13 finale on Thursday, Oct. 29. “We had to learn, like, within an hour, an hour before we started filming or so.”
In the scene, Kelly’s Devil shares a tango with Lange’s Constance Langdon, who wears a striking red gown inside an elaborate, candlelit room. During their flirtatious exchange, Constance admits she sometimes feels trapped in the house and questions the decisions that led her there.
“I do feel like a butterfly trapped in a spider web in this house,” she says.
The conversation takes a playful turn when Constance suggests she could rule alongside the Devil, asking to become his “mistress of the damned for all time.” However, their romantic moment takes a shocking turn when the Devil reveals why they can never be together, telling Constance, “I’m your father,” before abruptly disappearing.
Despite the dramatic nature of the scene, Kelly says filming the dance sequence was filled with laughter. “That was a great experience, learning to tango with Jessica Lange,” he says. “While we were filming it, we’d have some missteps, and it was just a lot of laughs. Just a great time on set.”
As for whether he had any dance experience to fall back on, Kelly doesn’t hesitate to admit his limitations. “No, no. I have two left feet,” he jokes.
For Kelly, stepping into the supernatural world of American Horror Story also meant sharing the screen with several longtime franchise favorites. “I had the great gift of working with Jessica Lange and Sarah Paulson and John Waters and Billie Lourd and, yeah, these American Horror Story royalty,” he says.
“It was excellent,” he continues. “I think just being able to work with them and watch them work and take these characters that they’ve been creating for years, and then see that brought to life in front of me was really, really cool.”
Kelly, who previously portrayed John F. Kennedy Jr. in Ryan Murphy’s Love Story , says the opportunity to play the Devil came after Murphy called him while the series was airing.
“The fact that he called me personally was pretty great,” Kelly recalls, explaining that Murphy gave him an overview of the premise before asking, “Would you want to play the Devil?” His response was immediate: “Yeah, absolutely.”
Unlike his portrayal of Kennedy, Kelly says playing a fictional character allowed him to take more creative liberties. “JFK Jr. was very much a box that I had to play within, and I loved doing that,” he explains. “I think creating a character as well was a new experience. There’s obviously a lot of writing about the Devil, but there are no factual points.”
He ultimately envisioned the character as “this kind of old, classic Hollywood, suave, sophisticated, debonair guy.”
“I didn’t really have to push too hard,” he adds. “He already knew the outcome of everything, and, you know, he was kind of one step ahead of the curve until he wasn’t.”
While mastering the tango proved difficult, Kelly says the experience of working with the star-studded cast made the entire production unforgettable.
“Any time spent with John Waters is hilarious,” he says. “ Sarah Paulson ’s amazing. Billie Lourd , Emma Roberts . Like, I really got to hang out with some super cool people, and people that I’ve looked up to for a very long time. The whole process of making it was memorable.”
American Horror Story is now streaming on Hulu.
